entries.note: DOI resolves (PMC3084838); quote verbatim in abstract and full text. But PLoS One RETRACTED this paper 2024-11-13 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0313936, PMID 39536007). Status/year stand; record the retraction, drop confidence to low, or cite a non-retracted 9E4 mouse source.

JAMA Neurol 75(10):1206, PMC6233845; quote verbatim in abstract. Untested holds: Lang 2022 and Pagano 2022 full texts both state target engagement was not measured; Schenk 2017 full text says CNS penetration 'remains to be demonstrated ... as is predicted by preclinical studies'.

Quote verbatim, but same retracted source (see engagement 1). Note is also wrong: Pagano 2021 (doi 10.3389/fneur.2021.705407, open access) says the PASADENA 1500 mg dose was set 'to yield exposure levels above those effective on alpha-synuclein pathology in the mouse model'.

Mov Disord 34(8):1154, PMC6771554, epub 2019-06-17; quote verbatim in Discussion (45-mg/kg hyphen normalised as stated). Untested holds: Lang 2022 full text confirms 'no dose-response relation was detected' and nobody compares exposures.

Quote verbatim (abstract/full text), but the source is retracted (PLoS One 2024-11-13); see engagement 1. Masliah 2005 Neuron (active immunisation) also carries a 2025-11-05 expression of concern. Keep 2011 untested; mark retraction.
Neurobiol Dis 124:276-288, epub 2018-10-28, print April 2019; quote verbatim in abstract (abstract only, Elsevier paywall). Model row for cinpanemab is correct; product_in_model true is right.

NEJM full text read (free after 6 months). Intro states the PFF-mouse prediction (motor impairment, striatal DAT density); Results null on MDS-UPDRS and DaT-SPECT; Discussion never mentions mice. Doody 2013 precedent gives contra 2022; comparison_stated true (one paper), no contrasting sentence.

Lancet 407(10544):2227-2240, PMID 42208564, May 2026; quote verbatim in abstract (abstract only). Registry 2025-12-02 confirmed. Once 2022 is contra this row is a continuation, not a status change; keep only as a fact carrier or drop.

Quote verbatim in Brys 2019 Discussion; 5-mm asymptomatic CVA, 135 mg/kg healthy volunteer, 'approximately 3-fold higher' than the phase II top dose all confirmed; source leaves causality open ('could not be excluded'), so untested with comparison_stated true is right.

missing: Dose cell, 2021 untested row: Pagano 2021 Front Neurol (doi 10.3389/fneur.2021.705407, PMC8518716) states PASADENA's 1500 mg dose was chosen 'to yield exposure levels above those effective on alpha-synuclein pathology in the mouse model' and both doses 'were expected to bind >90% of pathological aggregated alpha-synuclein in the central nervous system'. That is a mouse-derived human exposure target for prasinezumab (Line D / Line 61 Thy1-alpha-syn mice, 9E4); still untested because CNS binding was never measured (Pagano 2022: 'we did not incorporate testing for target engagement because such tests are not well developed').

Engagement cell, optional 2022 untested row with a primary-source quote: Lang 2022 'a limitation of the trial is that we were unable to measure target engagement of the drug to verify clearance of alpha-synuclein' (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2203395) and/or Pagano 2022 'we did not incorporate testing for target engagement because such tests are not well developed' (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2202867).

Retraction: Masliah 2011 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0019338) retracted by PLoS One 2024-11-13 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0313936, PMID 39536007); cited on three rows with confidence high and no mention. Non-retracted alternatives for the 9E4 model claim: Games 2014 J Neurosci 34:9441 (not verified by me) or the Line D / Line 61 description in Pagano 2021.

Safety note: Lang 2022 reports transient ischaemic attack as the most common serious adverse event in the extension (4 of 353 cinpanemab-treated, 1%), which echoes the Brys 2019 vascular event; no source compares it with toxicology, so no status change, but the draft's 'headache, nasopharyngitis, falls' omits it.
Top-level context note ('no accessible primary source sets the mouse prediction beside the patient result') must be rewritten if efficacy flips to contra.
Whone 2022 NEJM editorial (doi 10.1056/NEJMe2207681) not read; as commentary it cannot set a status under rule 1.
rule_questions: Does contra require the primary source to contain an explicit model-vs-patient sentence? Neither NEJM Discussion revisits the mouse (both Introductions state the mouse result; Lang's Discussion blames intervention timing and extracellular N-terminal targeting). If the Doody 2013 precedent (trial paper plus drafter juxtaposition) is the standard, Lang 2022 sets contra in 2022 and is the stronger case because the same paper states the mouse claim and reports the matched endpoints (motor, striatal DAT) null. If an explicit sentence is required, this stays untested and ad-amyloid 2013 should be re-scored for consistency.

comparison_stated semantics: a single source carrying the model claim (Intro) and the patient result (Results) on matched endpoints, with no contrasting sentence -- true or false? I propose true (the drafter is not juxtaposing two sources) but the brief's 'side by side' could be read as requiring an explicit contrast.
Retracted model source: does a 2024 retraction void the 2011 strip opening (model_first_use_year), or does the model's use stand while the citation is replaced? The brief is silent.
One entry per change of status: once 2022 is contra, is the 2026 PADOVA row (same status) allowed purely as a registry_date fact carrier, or must it be dropped?

Scope of the contra: Lang 2022 contradicts the PFF model with the product itself dosed (product_in_model true). The prasinezumab/Thy1 comparison is weaker (mouse readouts were aggregates, gliosis, water-maze and beam; patient readouts MDS-UPDRS and DaT-SPECT). Should the row name only the PFF model as contradicted, with Thy1 left untested, or does 'best model in the context' carry one status for both?
